office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Democratic incumbent Shelley Kloba, in the House since 2017, faces Republican Cliff Moon, a construction-business owner who edged Democrat Jenne Alderks for the second primary slot. Kloba defends the 2026 Millionaires Tax and her AI and privacy record; Moon runs on property-tax relief, police funding and curriculum transparency.

candidates.summary: Incumbent State Representative since 2017 and Vice-Chair of the House Technology, Economic Development, and Veterans Committee, focused on data privacy, AI guardrails and tax-code changes.
highlights: Voted for ESSB 6346, the 2026 tax on income over $1 million, and calls it the start of correcting an upside-down tax code [S2][S5]
Prime sponsor of the People's Privacy Act (HB 1671) and a data-broker registry bill [S8]
Original sponsor of HB 1296 (2025), which amended the I-2081 parental-rights list [S7]

taxes.basis: Voted for the Millionaires Tax and defends it and the capital gains tax as correcting an upside-down tax code, pledging further 'fair tax' bills.

spending.basis: Platform emphasizes fully funding K-12, behavioral-health access and renewable-energy investment rather than audits or restraint.

safety.basis: Highlights crisis-responder teams and crisis treatment centers law enforcement can use instead of jail or the ER.

climate.basis: Supports reducing dependence on fossil fuels, renewable-energy investment and green jobs in pamphlet and website; endorsed by Sierra Club.

experience.basis: Nine years in the House, committee vice-chair, bills enacted; opponent has never held office beyond PCO.

healthcare.basis: Says health care is 'a right, not a privilege', should never be tied to employment, and calls for 'getting rid of the middleman'; no explicit single-payer proposal.

social.basis: Endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates and Washington Stonewall Democrats; no statement of her own beyond protecting civil rights.

parental-rights.basis: Original sponsor of and yes vote on ESHB 1296, which modified and narrowed parts of the I-2081 parental-rights list.

tech.basis: Record centers data-privacy and AI regulation: People's Privacy Act, data-broker registry bill, AI consumer-harm work; says AI should not exploit people for profit.

candidates.summary: Republican construction-business owner and Precinct Committee Officer running on property-tax relief, police funding, spending audits and curriculum transparency.
highlights: Supports property-tax caps and senior exemptions and lower B&O taxes for small operators [S2]
Supports fully funding police, with crisis response as 'a complement to — not replacement for' police [S2]
Opposes 'one-size-fits-all mandates from Olympia' on housing [S2]

taxes.basis: Pamphlet and website center tax relief: property-tax caps, lower B&O taxes and resisting tax increases.

spending.basis: Says the state should spend wisely and audit programs that aren't delivering results.

safety.basis: Runs on fully funding police and accountability in the courts, while also backing mental-health crisis response as a complement.

housing.basis: Supports removing barriers to housing production and local control over development; no public-housing or tenant-protection proposals.

local-control.basis: Explicitly opposes one-size-fits-all mandates from Olympia and wants local communities to shape their own development.

climate.basis: Wants environmental policies that do not destroy jobs or make energy unaffordable; no stated climate-policy commitments.

experience.basis: No elected office beyond Precinct Committee Officer; runs on a business background against a nine-year incumbent.

parental-rights.basis: Says parents should raise their children and supports 'parental involvement, transparency in curriculum'; no specific notification or opt-out proposal.
